newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen recovers after slide, 111.60 seen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen recovers after slide, 111.60 seen.

text.p: Dollar/yen's quick reversal from an early slide below 110.80 on Friday surprised chartists and some say the dollar could move higher in the short-term.

"Dollar/yen is a little iffy," said Ken Boyer, foreign exchange analyst at MMS International. "I still think it's vulnerable on the downside, but we stabilized in the day after confirming Fibonacci support at 110.60 this morning."
The dollar hit 110.55 yen -- the 50-percent retracement of the 106.30 to 114.91 July to October rise -- on Friday after key support near last week's low at 110.72 yen was punctured.

But while short-term traders who sold dollars when support broke this morning were forced to cover after dollar/yen's surprise rebound, intermediate and long-term dollar bears need not worry unless the dollar surpasses 112 yen.

"If we stay between 111 and 112 yen, people are still going to be bearish," said Craig Coatney, a proprietary trader and director at Bank of Montreal. "If we creep above 112 people are still going to want to be short, but are going to be concerned the correction is going to be little higher."
The dollar should test 111.60 yen soon and the market will probably look to reestablish shorts ahead of 112 yen, said Coatney. But stop-loss orders should be left at 112.50, he added.
Some daily technical studies turned bullish after the dollar/yen selloff faltered, but analysts do not expect traders to suddenly embrace a bullish outlook.
"There is some positive divergence on a daily basis," Coatney said. "Does that mean you buy it? Maybe if you're brave."
Meanwhile, dollar/mark should make its way towards trendline resistance at 1.5145, with strong support between 1.5000 and 1.5030 expected to limit the downside, analysts said.
"Due to the key reversal on Tuesday, to me the charts are looking a little bit firmer so I think we will get above 1.5145 and head towards 1.5250 on upside," said Boyer.
At 1400 EST on Friday, the dollar was quoted at 1.5105/15 marks up from 1.5040/50 at the open and at 111.25/30 up from 110.55/65.
